summary.anthropology: Community-owned living archive of the neighborhood's cultures, recorded by paid community ethnographers; shapes programming and identifies who and what needs protection.
summary.protection: The plan produces neighborhood value; part of that value is committed, in advance, to protecting the residents, businesses and cultural practitioners that rising value puts at risk. Promotion and protection are coupled: the hub only scales what draws demand when protection is funded and the displacement indicators are stable.
summary.membership: A two-sided district partnership in which social members and capital members hold equal standing, and protection of vulnerable residents and legacy businesses is a core purpose of the district rather than something it leaves out.

prohibited_uses: sale or licensing of records without community approval

protection.problem: Successful cultural reactivation raises foot traffic and land values, which raises rents and eviction pressure on low-income residents, legacy businesses and artists. Displacement shifts costs elsewhere in the city (shelter, health, lost work and community ties).

executed_evictions.source: NYC Open Data - Evictions (6z8x-wfk4), marshal-executed only; undercounts informal displacement

HDFC boards on Allen and Rivington

items: Extend or confirm Certification of No Harassment (CONH) coverage for buildings in Community District 3 (verify current coverage)

coupling_rule.description: Promotion scales only with protection. Tourism-facing marketing and new revenue lines expand only when the continuity fund meets its target and displacement indicators are stable or improving.
conditions_for_expansion: executed residential evictions in 400 m ring not above baseline average
no increase in legacy-business closures year over year
coupling_rule.pause_trigger: If conditions fail for two consecutive quarters, the cultural council may pause new promotional campaigns and redirect surplus to the continuity fund

city_level_case.argument: Preventing displacement saves public money: rehousing and shelter cost far more than keeping people housed.

reference_figures.source: Win NYC, 'More Than a Moral Choice' (Feb 2026)

city_level_case.link_to_parks: The general fund that receives Parks concession fees also pays shelter costs; protection is a fiscal benefit to the same budget.

standard_bid.governance: Board weighted to property owners; residents and tenants hold minority seats

this_model.funding: Capital pledges scaled to capacity plus social contributions valued as membership dues
this_model.governance: Equal capital and social halves; resident majority on protection decisions
this_model.purpose: Cultural continuity, protection of residents and legacy businesses, and shared economic uplift

capital_self_interest_case.summary: Capital members invest in the district's distinctiveness; displacement of the people who create that distinctiveness erodes the asset they paid for.
